sanskrit: kim indrasya parihitaṃ kim agneḥ kiṃ viṣṇos tvaṣṭur varuṇasya vāsaḥ | bṛhaspater uta somasya rājñaḥ kiṃ vasānā maruto varṣayantu ||
english: What is the garment of Indra, what of Agni, what the raiment of Viṣṇu, of Tvaṣṭṛ, of Varuṇa? What of Bṛhaspati and of King Soma — clad in what shall the Maruts let the rain fall?

sanskrit: dhātū rudrasya kiṃ vāyor vājināṃ vasanaṃ mahat | kiṃ pūṣā brahmaṇaspatir viśve devāś ca bibhrati ||
english: What are the elements of Rudra? What is the great garment of Vāyu, of the swift ones? What do Pūṣan, Brahmaṇaspati, and all the gods bear and sustain?

sanskrit: kiṃ devānāṃ paridhānaṃ samānaṃ yasminn eṣāṃ sāṃmanasyaṃ babhūva | kva rātrī niviśate kvāhaḥ kvedam abhraṃ bhavati yat sameti vyeti ca ||
english: What is the common garment of the gods, wherein their harmony was established? Where does Night settle to rest, and where does Day — where does this cloud that gathers and disperses come to be?

sanskrit: katamenāpo divam udvahanti kaḥ samenodayanena netā | vātasya tvā vidyutāṃ stanayitnur apāṃ pṛcchāmy ayanāny agneḥ ||
english: By what means do the waters bear up the sky? Who is the guide that leads with equal rising? Of the wind, of the lightnings, of the thunderer — I ask of thee the paths of the waters and of Agni.

sanskrit: pṛcchāmi tvā pṛṣatīṃ rohiṇīṃ ca vatsaṃ pṛcchāmi saha mātaraṃ tvā | indraṃ tvānu pṛcchāmi sākṣāt sabhānāṃ ca sabhāpatim ||
english: I ask thee of Pṛṣatī and of Rohiṇī; I ask thee of the calf together with its mother. I ask thee directly of Indra, and of the lord of assemblies among the assemblies.

sanskrit: ko vayasām adadhān nāmāni kaḥ paśūnāṃ kaḥ sarpāṇāṃ devajanā ya āsan | ko 'sya jantor adadhād brūhi nas tat ||
english: Who assigned the names of birds, who of cattle, who of serpents among those who were the divine folk? Who bestowed the name upon this living creature — declare that to us.

sanskrit: kati rohāḥ svar ā rohayanti yebhī rohito divam āruroha | rāṣṭrabhṛtaḥ kṣatrabhṛto vasubhṛto vasudānavo vasuyavaḥ ||
english: How many ascents cause one to mount to the light, by which the Rohita mounted to heaven — bearers of kingship, bearers of dominion, bearers of riches, givers of riches, those for whom grain is wealth?

sanskrit: kaś caturdhā vi kramate mahitvā kaṃ rakṣanti kavayo 'pramādam | puruṣaṃ tvānu pṛcchāmi sākṣān mṛtyor aṅgāni kati tāni vettha ||
english: Who strides forth fourfold in his greatness? Whom do the seers guard with unwearied vigilance? I ask thee directly of the Puruṣa — how many are the limbs of Death? Dost thou know them?

sanskrit: yaṃ siṣeva vṛṣabhaś carṣaṇīṇām indro vajram ahīnā spardhamānaḥ | yena vṛtraṃ maghavā saṃpipeśa taṃ naḥ pra brūhi yadi taṃ pravettha ||
english: That thunderbolt which the bull of all peoples, Indra, fashioned, rivalling the serpents — wherewith the bounteous one crushed Vṛtra — declare that to us, if indeed thou knowest it.

sanskrit: kaḥ parvatānām adadhān nāmāni ko vanaspatīnām adadhād oṣadhīnām | pṛcchāmi tvā bhuvanasya nābhiṃ gāṃ tvā pṛcchāmi katamāni sākṣāt ||
english: Who assigned the names of mountains, who bestowed the names of forest lords and plants? I ask thee of the navel of the world; I ask thee of the cow — which ones directly?

sanskrit: devatalpā devakośāḥ kveha tān naḥ pra brūhi yadi tān pravettha | pṛcchāmi tvā garagiraḥ kiyanto yebhyo 'gnir havyaṃ vahati prajānan hutaṃ martyair amṛto martyebhyaḥ ||
english: The divine couches, the divine treasuries — where are they here? Declare them to us if thou knowest them. I ask thee how many are the altars of oblation, from which Agni, the immortal, knowing it, carries the offering poured by mortals on behalf of mortals.

sanskrit: svapne ya ekas tamasā sahaity aṅgāni gṛhṇan puruṣasya cakṣuḥ | sa prātar eti tamasā punaḥ sa hā jyotir eti kva sadadeti ||
english: He who in dream comes alone with darkness, seizing the limbs and the eye of a man — he departs at dawn with the darkness again; he goes toward the light — where, tell me, does he settle?

sanskrit: vratapatim adhipatiṃ madhukṛtā madhupatim | devāṃs tvā sarvān pṛcchāmy ahutādaś ca te kati ||
english: The lord of vows, the overlord, the maker of sweetness, the lord of honey — I ask thee of all the gods; and those who feed on the unoffered oblation — how many are they?

sanskrit: ko 'ntarikṣāt pari paśyatīdaṃ yasmād agra indriyaṃ saṃbabhūva | mahat sa kasmād abhayaṃ bibhāya kasya yuktasyāsyā srakvāl lohitaṃ parāpatat tat kveha ||
english: Who gazes round upon this from the mid-air, from whom at first vital power arose? That great one — from whom did he fear, becoming fearless? From the corner of whose mouth, when yoked, did blood flow forth? Where indeed is that?

sanskrit: ittham eke pravrajantīttham eke dakṣiṇāḥ pratyañca udañcaḥ prāñco 'bhi vrajanty eke | teṣāṃ sarveṣām iha saṅgatiḥ sākaṃ sa eko bhūtaś carati prajānan ||
english: Thus some go forth, and thus some others — southward, westward, northward, eastward some advance. The meeting point of all of them here together — he, having become one, moves about knowing all.

sanskrit: marīcir āsīt sā manasaḥ sam abhavat | sā pravīyata sā garbham adhatta | sa garbho 'vardhata sa vṛddho 'bravīj jāyā iti | tasyai prajāpatir ajuhot svadhiṣṭhānā ceti svadhicaraṇā ceti | prajāpatiḥ sasṛje kapāle vijihīthāṃ mā mā saṃ tāptaṃ mahāntaṃ lokam abhipaśyamāne so 'jāyata tasya jātasya dyāvāpṛthivī pārśve āstāṃ samudrau kukṣī sūryācandramāsāv akṣī virāṭ śiraḥ | tasmāj jātāt sarve pāpmāno vijante sarve asmāt pāpmāno vijante ya evaṃ veda ||
english: A mote of light there was; it came together out of the mind. It spread abroad; it held an embryo. That embryo grew; grown, it said: "Wife!" To her Prajāpati offered oblation, saying "Thou who art firmly established" and "Thou who movest firmly." Prajāpati fashioned two bowls: "Part asunder; do not scorch me — looking upon the great world" — and from them he was born. Of that one born, Heaven-and-Earth were the two flanks, the two oceans were the two hollows, Sun-and-Moon were the two eyes, the Virāj was the head. From that one thus born all evils flee; all evils flee from him who knows this.
